correctness.rationale: The formula C_theta-uv=theta (u f(u))(v f(v))/(1-theta f(u)f(v)) is exact. Hoeffding integration by parts identifies this kernel with the centered one-step covariance form. Positive theta with theta f(0)^2<1 yields a uniformly differentiable Gram series and a trace-class nonnegative operator; Vandermonde linear independence on any distinct nodes gives infinite positive rank, and the spectral measure on [0,1] implies complete monotonicity at every lag. For theta=-a<0, the Cauchy determinant of every m-by-m kernel sample equals (-1)^{m(m+1)/2} a^{m(m+1)/2} times a strictly positive factor; leading pivot signs (-1)^j give precisely floor(m/2) positive and ceil(m/2) negative eigenvalues. Smooth derivative-bump approximation transfers arbitrarily large signed subspaces to the compact Markov operator, proving infinitely many nonzero eigenvalues of each sign. Finite determinant calculations were replayed from the included checker through m=6 and a two-node exponential example was numerically corroborated; the all-m proof is analytic. The copula and positive-denominator assumptions are explicit.

value.rationale: This is an exact infinite-dimensional structure theorem for a motivated, published class of copula Markov chains, not a finite table or numerical increment. It determines the sign phase of the full centered operator on both sides of the independence parameter, exact inertia for every finite observation grid, all-observable complete monotonicity in one regime, and alternating modes in the other. It shows why negative quadrant dependence of a stationary pair cannot be substituted for nonpositive eigenvalues or negative covariance of arbitrary nonmonotone statistics. The distinction is pertinent to serial-covariance and spectral assumptions in count-free dependence modeling.
